issues.legal_issue: An alleged contract and equitable part performance do not transfer title to property where the required registered instrument is absent and the statutory conditions for part-performance protection are not satisfied.
material_facts: The claimant’s father allegedly agreed to inherit the property in return for marrying a relative of the property owner and managing the owner’s property.
The claimant relied on the alleged agreement to claim title after the owner’s death, but no registered instrument transferring the property was executed.
Specific performance of the alleged agreement was not sought in the proceeding.
The statutory requirements for protection based on part performance were not satisfied.
issues.conclusion: The alleged contract and equitable considerations did not confer title on the claimant or his heirs. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the English doctrine of equity of part performance could be applied in India only where that section’s requirements were satisfied. Equity could not override a statutory requirement that title be conferred only by a registered instrument. The Court relied on Ariff v. Jadunath Majumdar (1931) and treated Challa Papi Reddi v. Challa Koti Reddi, Bhalla Nahana v. Prabhu Hari, Asita Mohan Ghosh Moulik v. Mohan Ghosh Moulik, and Venkatayyamma Rao v. Appa Rao as inapplicable to the issue before it.

rule.if: property_title_proceeding and contract_based_title_claim and no_registered_transfer_instrument and not part_performance_conditions_met

predicates.property_title_proceeding: The proceeding concerned a civil claim to title to property.
predicates.contract_based_title_claim: A claimant relied on an alleged agreement as the basis for acquiring title to the property.
predicates.no_registered_transfer_instrument: The parties did not execute a registered instrument transferring the property to the claimant.
predicates.part_performance_conditions_met: The facts satisfied the legal conditions for protection based on part performance.

issues.definition: When a civil property-title proceeding involves a contract-based title claim, no registered transfer instrument, and unmet conditions for part-performance protection, equity does not confer title on the claimant.
